sections.heading: The title and the central idea
bullets: एतद् उपास्यम् means 'THIS is worthy of worship'; उपास्यम् is a gerundive (कृत्य-प्रत्यय यत् on उप-आस्), 'that which ought to be worshipped', like कर्तव्यम् 'that which ought to be done'.
The 'this' is honest work itself: the chapter's thesis is कर्म एव पूजा — sincere labour done with श्रद्धा is the truest form of worship.
The chapter upholds the dignity of labour (श्रमस्य गौरवम्): the farmer's plough, the potter's wheel and the student's study are all altars; no honest work is low.
Even the title models grammar: एतत् + उपास्यम् → एतद् उपास्यम् by जश्त्व-सन्धि (त् → द् before a vowel).

sections.heading: The story: two 'worshippers' of Dharmapura
bullets: Somadatta performed loud, showy puja from morning to evening (बाह्याडम्बर) but did no work: his field lay dry, his house dilapidated, his family miserable — and he turned away a hungry guest saying 'this is my puja time'.
The farmer Dharmapala worked his field as worship — 'my farming is my puja, my sweat-drops the flowers, my labour the mantra' — fed the hungry and honoured guests.

The visiting sannyasi tested both, then pointed to Dharmapala's work-sanctified plough and sweat-moistened earth and declared: एतद् उपास्यम् — THIS deserves worship; कर्म एव पूजा, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना.
Somadatta, ashamed, began to work sincerely from that day, and in time the village prospered — showing that reform is possible and that work uplifts the whole community.

sections.heading: The karma verses and their message
bullets: Gita 2.47 कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते: your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits — and do not slide into inaction (मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि).
Gita 3.19 तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर: perform obligatory work constantly and without attachment; the unattached worker attains the Highest (परम्).
Gita 18.46 स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य: worshipping the all-pervading Lord THROUGH one's own work, a person attains perfection (सिद्धि) — the scriptural core of 'work is worship'.
Isha Upanishad 2 कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः: one should wish to live a hundred years doing works; done rightly, action does not stain the doer.
The subhashita उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः: effort, not daydreaming, accomplishes tasks — even a lion must hunt.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धि: एतत् + उपास्यम् = एतद् उपास्यम् and तस्मात् + असक्तः = तस्मादसक्तः (जश्त्व); कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव and हि + आचरन् = ह्याचरन् (यण्); न + अन्यथा = नान्यथा (दीर्घ); जिजीविषेत् + शतम् = जिजीविषेच्छतम् (श्चुत्व).

समास: कर्मयोगः = कर्मणा योगः (तृतीया-तत्पुरुष); कर्मफलम् = कर्मणः फलम् and स्वेदबिन्दवः = स्वेदस्य बिन्दवः (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष); ग्रामवासिनः = ग्रामे वासिनः (सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष); बाह्याडम्बरः = बाह्यः आडम्बरः (कर्मधारय); क्षुधार्तः = क्षुधा आर्तः (तृतीया-तत्पुरुष).

विभक्ति: श्रद्धया / उद्यमेन / स्वकर्मणा (तृतीया 'by/with'); क्षुधितेभ्यः (चतुर्थी 'to', with दान); तस्मात् दिनात् (पञ्चमी 'from'); सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य (षष्ठी 'of'); क्षेत्रे, फलेषु, अकर्मणि (सप्तमी 'in').
लकाराः: लट् करोति/गच्छति (present); लङ् अपश्यत्/अभवत् (past); लोट् समाचर/पश्यत (command); विधिलिङ् जिजीविषेत्/कुर्यात् (should).
कृत्य-प्रत्ययाः (gerundives): उपास्यम्, कार्यम्, कर्तव्यम् — all meaning 'ought to be —ed'; the title word itself is a gerundive.

sections.heading: Values and application to life
bullets: True devotion is measured by service, not by noise: Somadatta's bell fed no one; Dharmapala's plough fed the village.
निष्काम कर्म — work without greed for reward — keeps the mind steady and the work pure; but detachment must never become an excuse for idleness.
For a student, sincere study done with shraddha IS karma-yoga; for every profession, honest skilled work offered to the good of all is worship.
Respect manual labour and those who do it — farmers, artisans, sanitation workers; contempt for labour contradicts the chapter's ideal of श्रमस्य गौरवम्.

key_takeaways: एतद् उपास्यम् = 'this is worthy of worship'; the chapter's answer to 'what deserves worship?' is honest work itself — कर्म एव पूजा.
उपास्यम् is a gerundive (उप-आस् + यत्), and the title shows जश्त्व-सन्धि: एतत् + उपास्यम् → एतद् उपास्यम्.
The story contrasts Somadatta's idle showy ritualism (बाह्याडम्बर) with Dharmapala's work-as-devotion; the sannyasi's verdict goes to the farmer's plough.
Gita 18.46 स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः — worshipping God through one's own work, one attains perfection.
Gita 2.47 and 3.19 teach निष्काम कर्म: your right is to the work, not its fruits — and never let 'detachment' become inaction.
Isha Upanishad 2 and उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति uphold the Vedic ideal of श्रम/उद्यम: live long working; effort, not wishes, accomplishes.
Service — feeding the hungry, honouring the guest, doing one's duty — is the real measure of worship; labour has dignity and no honest work is low.

glossary.definition: 'Worthy of worship / to be served devotedly' — gerundive of उप + आस् with the कृत्य suffix यत्; the key word of the title.
The yoga (discipline) of action: doing one's duty skilfully, sincerely and without attachment to results, as taught in the Bhagavad Gita.
'Work itself is worship' — the chapter's central teaching: honest labour offered with faith is the truest form of adoration.
The dignity of labour: the principle that no honest work is low and that physical labour deserves respect.
Outward show, showy display (बाह्यः आडम्बरः, कर्मधारय) — Somadatta's noisy but empty ritualism.
Faith, devoted sincerity; श्रद्धया (तृतीया) = 'with faith' — the spirit in which Dharmapala worked.
Desireless action — work performed without craving for its fruit, the ideal of Gita 2.47.
One's own work or allotted duty; स्वकर्मणा (तृतीया) 'by one's own work' — the instrument of worship in Gita 18.46.
Effort, industry, diligence; by उद्यम tasks succeed (उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि), not by mere wishes (मनोरथ).
Adoration, devoted worship; in the sannyasi's words, सेवा एव आराधना — service itself is adoration.
A renunciant monk; in the story, the impartial visitor who tests both men and declares the true worshipper.
The plough; Dharmapala's कर्मपूतं हलम् ('work-sanctified plough') becomes the object the sannyasi calls worthy of worship.
A gerundive suffix (यत्, ण्यत्, तव्यत्, अनीयर्) meaning 'ought to be —ed', as in उपास्यम्, कार्यम्, कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्.
Consonant sandhi in which a voiceless stop becomes voiced before a vowel or voiced sound, e.g. एतत् + उपास्यम् = एतद् उपास्यम्.
The optative mood ('should/ought'), e.g. जिजीविषेत् 'one should wish to live', कुर्यात् 'one should do'.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — एतद् उपास्यम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 7)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the story and the verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question: What does the title एतद् उपास्यम् mean, and how is the word उपास्यम् formed?
questions.answer: The title means 'THIS is worthy of worship'. उपास्यम् is a gerundive formed from उप + आस् (to worship, serve devotedly) with the कृत्य suffix यत्, giving the sense 'that which ought to be worshipped' — like कर्तव्यम् 'that which ought to be done'. In the chapter the 'this' is honest work itself.
questions.explanation: Title meaning plus the कृत्य-प्रत्यय formation.

questions.question: Describe in 3-4 sentences how Somadatta and Dharmapala each spent their day, and what resulted for their households.
questions.answer: Somadatta spent the whole day in showy worship — ringing the bell loudly, offering flowers, reciting mantras — but did no work; so his field was dry, his house dilapidated and his family miserable. Dharmapala rose early, remembered God briefly and worked his field, doing japa in his mind while ploughing; he treated his farming as his puja. His field was green with crops, his house clean and his family content, and he fed the hungry and honoured guests.
questions.explanation: The story's central contrast: idle ritualism vs work-as-devotion, with their visible results.

questions.question: To what did the sannyasi point when he said एतद् उपास्यम्, and what did he mean?
questions.answer: He pointed to Dharmapala's work-sanctified plough (कर्मपूतं हलम्) and the sweat-moistened earth. He meant that sincere work itself deserves worship: कर्म एव पूजा, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना — the true worshipper is the one who does his own work with shraddha, not the one who makes an outward show.
questions.explanation: The story's climax interprets the title.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) एतद् उपास्यम् (b) तस्मादसक्तः, and name the sandhi.
questions.answer: (a) एतद् उपास्यम् = एतत् + उपास्यम् — the voiceless त् becomes voiced द् before the vowel उ (जश्त्व-सन्धि). (b) तस्मादसक्तः = तस्मात् + असक्तः — the same जश्त्व rule (त् → द् before the vowel अ).
questions.explanation: Both illustrate जश्त्व: a final voiceless stop voices before a vowel.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role of each word as used in the lesson: श्रद्धया, क्षुधितेभ्यः, क्षेत्रे.
questions.answer: श्रद्धया = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'with faith/devotion'. क्षुधितेभ्यः = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'to the hungry' (recipient of giving, दान). क्षेत्रे = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in the field'.
questions.explanation: तृतीया shows means/manner, चतुर्थी the recipient, सप्तमी the place.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of Gita 18.46 — 'यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥' — with its अन्वय, and show how the story of Dharmapala embodies this verse.
questions.answer:
अन्वय: यतः भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः, येन इदं सर्वं ततम्, तं स्वकर्मणा अभ्यर्च्य मानवः सिद्धिं विन्दति । Meaning: From whom all beings arise and by whom all this universe is pervaded — worshipping Him THROUGH one's own work (स्वकर्मणा अभ्यर्च्य), a human being attains perfection (सिद्धि). The verse teaches that one's own honest duty, offered to God, is itself an act of worship; no separate ritual is required.
Dharmapala embodies this: his farming is his puja ('मम कृषिः एव मम पूजा'), his sweat-drops his flowers, his labour his mantra. He worships through his own work — and attains 'siddhi' in visible form: a green field, a content family, the honour of feeding the hungry, and finally the sannyasi's recognition that HIS work, not Somadatta's noisy ritual, is worthy of worship.
questions.explanation: Anvaya, translation and the mapping verse-to-story are all expected.

questions.question: 'Detachment must never become an excuse for idleness.' Discuss this statement using Gita 2.47 (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते ... मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि) and the character of Somadatta.
questions.answer:
Gita 2.47 has two warnings, not one. First: your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन) — do not work only for reward. Second, and equally important: मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि — 'let your attachment not be to INACTION'. Detachment from results must not slide into detachment from work itself.
Somadatta illustrates the danger: he treated work as beneath him ('कर्म तु सामान्यजनानां कृते') and hid his idleness behind a screen of ritual. His 'devotion' produced nothing — a dry field, a suffering family, a hungry guest turned away. True karma-yoga is the opposite: like Dharmapala, one works constantly and sincerely, while remaining unattached to reward. Renunciation in the Gita is renunciation of selfish craving, not of effort.
questions.explanation: Requires connecting the verse's second half (मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि) to Somadatta's idleness.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः' and state which text it comes from.
questions.answer: 'Doing works alone should one wish to live here (in this world) a hundred years.' It is from the Isha Upanishad (mantra 2). It teaches the Vedic ideal that a full human life is a working life — one should desire long life precisely in order to keep doing one's duties.
questions.explanation: जिजीविषेत् = 'one should wish to live' (विधिलिङ्); शतं समाः = a hundred years.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: बाह्याडम्बरः, हलम्, स्वेदबिन्दवः, क्षुधार्तः, समृद्धः, उद्यमेन.
questions.answer: बाह्याडम्बरः = outward show / showy display; हलम् = plough; स्वेदबिन्दवः = drops of sweat; क्षुधार्तः = tormented by hunger; समृद्धः = prosperous; उद्यमेन = by effort/industry.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the story and the subhashita.

questions.question: Dissolve (विग्रह) the compounds and name the समास: (a) कर्मयोगः (b) ग्रामवासिनः.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मयोगः = कर्मणा योगः — union/discipline THROUGH action → तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः. (b) ग्रामवासिनः = ग्रामे वासिनः — dwellers IN the village → सप्तमी-तत्पुरुषः.
questions.explanation: The hidden case of the first member names the तत्पुरुष type.

questions.question: The title एतद् उपास्यम् means
questions.answer: this is worthy of worship
questions.explanation: एतद् = this; उपास्यम् = worthy of being worshipped/served (gerundive of उप-आस्).

questions.question: According to the chapter, the 'this' (एतद्) that truly deserves worship is
questions.answer: honest work done with faith
questions.explanation: The chapter's thesis is कर्म एव पूजा — sincere labour itself is worship.

questions.question: The word उपास्यम् is derived from the root आस् with the prefix उप and the suffix
questions.answer: यत् (कृत्य-प्रत्यय)
questions.explanation: उप + आस् + यत् = उपास्यम्, a gerundive meaning 'that which ought to be worshipped'.

questions.question: उपास्यम् belongs to the same grammatical family ('ought to be —ed') as
questions.answer: कर्तव्यम्
questions.explanation: Both are कृत्य (gerundive) forms: उपास्यम् 'to be worshipped', कर्तव्यम् 'to be done'. गत्वा is an absolutive, पठन् a present participle, गच्छति a finite verb.

questions.question: The central teaching of the chapter is summarised in the phrase
questions.answer: कर्म एव पूजा
questions.explanation: 'Work itself is worship' — the sannyasi's own words in the story.

questions.question: श्रमस्य गौरवम्, an ideal upheld by this chapter, means
questions.answer: the dignity of labour
questions.explanation: श्रमस्य = of labour; गौरवम् = dignity/honour: no honest work is low.

questions.question: Why is the neuter pronoun एतद् ('this'), rather than एषः ('he'), apt in the title?
options: The sannyasi points to work itself (the plough, the labour), not to a person
Neuter pronouns are compulsory in all Sanskrit titles
एषः cannot be used in prose
The villagers did not know Dharmapala's name
questions.answer: The sannyasi points to work itself (the plough, the labour), not to a person
questions.explanation: The verdict honours karma itself — the work-sanctified plough — not merely the individual; hence the neuter 'this'.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the sannyasi's equations in the story?
options: श्रमः एव मन्त्रः; सेवा एव आराधना
धनम् एव पूजा; बलम् एव मन्त्रः
मौनम् एव सेवा; निद्रा एव आराधना
यज्ञः एव कर्म; दानम् एव फलम्
questions.answer: श्रमः एव मन्त्रः; सेवा एव आराधना
questions.explanation: The sannyasi declares: कर्म एव पूजा, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना.

questions.question: For a Class 12 student, the chapter's ideal of कर्मयोग would best translate into
options: studying sincerely with full attention, treating study itself as worship
skipping study to attend more rituals
studying only when an examination reward is certain
leaving studies to serve in a temple
questions.answer: studying sincerely with full attention, treating study itself as worship
questions.explanation: One's own duty (स्वकर्म) done with श्रद्धा is worship; for a student that duty is study.

questions.question: The story of the chapter is set in a village named
questions.answer: धर्मपुरम्
questions.explanation: धर्मपुरं नाम रम्यः ग्रामः आसीत् — the story opens in Dharmapura.

questions.question: In the story, the man who performed only showy worship all day was
questions.answer: सोमदत्तः
questions.explanation: Somadatta rang the bell, offered flowers and recited mantras but did no work.

questions.question: धर्मपालः, the true worshipper of the story, was by occupation a
questions.answer: कृषकः (farmer)
questions.explanation: धर्मपालः नाम कृषकः न्यवसत् — he worked his field as his worship.

questions.question: What did Dharmapala do while driving the plough (हलं चालयन्)?
options: He did japa in his mind
questions.answer: He did japa in his mind
questions.explanation: सः हलं चालयन् एव मनसा जपं करोति स्म — outward work, inward remembrance.

questions.question: In Dharmapala's own words, his 'flowers' of worship were
questions.answer: his drops of sweat (स्वेदबिन्दवः)
questions.explanation: 'मम कृषिः एव मम पूजा, स्वेदबिन्दवः एव पुष्पाणि' — sweat-drops are the flowers of his puja.

questions.question: How did Somadatta treat the hungry sannyasi who came to his house?
options: He turned him away, saying it was his puja time
He fed him a full meal
He gave him money but no food
He asked him to wait in the field
questions.answer: He turned him away, saying it was his puja time
questions.explanation: 'पूजासमयः अयम् । मां मा बाधस्व' इति उक्त्वा तं निष्कासितवान् — ritual without compassion.

questions.question: What did the sannyasi see at Dharmapala's field?
options: Earth watered by labour, well-fed cattle and cheerful workers
A dry field and broken plough
A temple with a golden bell
questions.answer: Earth watered by labour, well-fed cattle and cheerful workers
questions.explanation: श्रमेण सिक्तां भूमिं, तृप्तान् पशून्, प्रसन्नान् कर्मकरान् च अपश्यत्.

questions.question: When the guest arrived, Dharmapala
options: set down his plough, honoured him and gave him food and water
asked him to come after the harvest
questions.answer: set down his plough, honoured him and gave him food and water
questions.explanation: स्वयं हलं त्यक्त्वा अतिथिं सत्कृत्य अन्नं पानीयं च अददात् — service before self.

questions.question: What was the condition of Somadatta's household as a result of his idleness?
options: Dry field, dilapidated house, miserable family
Green field, clean house, content family
The story does not describe his household
questions.answer: Dry field, dilapidated house, miserable family
questions.explanation: तस्य क्षेत्रं शुष्कम् आसीत्, गृहं जीर्णम्, कुटुम्बं च दुःखितम्.

questions.question: How does the story end for Somadatta?
options: Ashamed, he began to work sincerely from that day
He left the village in anger
He continued his showy worship unchanged
questions.answer: Ashamed, he began to work sincerely from that day
questions.explanation: सोमदत्तः लज्जितः अभवत् ... श्रद्धया कर्म कर्तुम् आरब्धवान् — and the village prospered.

questions.question: The central contrast of the story is between
options: idle showy ritualism and sincere work done as devotion
questions.answer: idle showy ritualism and sincere work done as devotion
questions.explanation: Somadatta's बाह्याडम्बर is set against Dharmapala's कर्म-रूपा पूजा.

questions.question: The word बाह्याडम्बरः, used of Somadatta's worship, indicates that his devotion was
options: an outward show without inner substance
questions.answer: an outward show without inner substance
questions.explanation: बाह्य (outer) + आडम्बर (display): loud bells and mantras with no work or compassion behind them.

questions.question: The hungry sannyasi's visit to both houses functions in the story as
options: a practical test that reveals each man's true devotion through action
a request for donations for a temple
an accident with no deeper meaning
a punishment sent to the village
questions.answer: a practical test that reveals each man's true devotion through action
questions.explanation: Words and rituals are tested against behaviour: Somadatta turns the guest away; Dharmapala feeds him.

questions.question: According to the sannyasi, without work and service, outward ritual show is
questions.answer: व्यर्थः (useless)
questions.explanation: कर्मणा सेवया च विना बाह्याडम्बरः व्यर्थः — his explicit verdict.

questions.question: The story attaches the epithet कर्मपूतम् ('sanctified by work') to the plough in order to suggest that
options: tools of honest labour acquire the sanctity usually attributed to ritual objects
the plough had been washed in the river
ploughs must be worshipped before temples are built
only iron objects can be sacred
questions.answer: tools of honest labour acquire the sanctity usually attributed to ritual objects
questions.explanation: The plough becomes like an idol — sanctified not by ritual but by sincere labour.

questions.question: Somadatta's saying 'कर्म तु सामान्यजनानां कृते' ('work is for ordinary people') reveals his
options: false pride and contempt for labour
questions.answer: false pride and contempt for labour
questions.explanation: His contempt for work is exactly the attitude the chapter refutes with श्रमस्य गौरवम्.

questions.question: The prosperity of the village at the end of the story shows that
options: when everyone works sincerely, the whole community flourishes
sannyasis bring wealth wherever they go
questions.answer: when everyone works sincerely, the whole community flourishes
questions.explanation: Once Somadatta too took to sincere work, कालेन सः ग्रामः समृद्धः अभवत्.

questions.question: Does the story condemn puja and ritual as such? Choose the best assessment.
options: No — it condemns ritual EMPTIED of work and compassion; Dharmapala himself remembers God and does japa
Yes — it declares all worship meaningless
Yes — it says only atheists can work well
No — it says ritual alone is sufficient without any work
questions.answer: No — it condemns ritual EMPTIED of work and compassion; Dharmapala himself remembers God and does japa
questions.explanation: Dharmapala also prays (स्मृत्वा, जपम्) — but his devotion flows into work and service, unlike Somadatta's hollow display.

questions.question: The sannyasi's declaration एतद् उपास्यम् was addressed to
questions.answer: the assembled villagers (ग्रामवासिनः)
questions.explanation: He answers the villagers' question 'who is the better worshipper?' publicly, pointing to the plough.

questions.question: The शब्दार्थ of हलम् is
questions.answer: plough
questions.explanation: हलम् = plough, Dharmapala's instrument of work and worship.

questions.question: The शब्दार्थ of कृषकः is
questions.answer: farmer
questions.explanation: कृषकः (from कृष् 'to plough') = one who tills, a farmer.

questions.question: स्वेदबिन्दवः means
questions.answer: drops of sweat
questions.explanation: स्वेदस्य बिन्दवः = drops of sweat — Dharmapala's 'flowers' of worship.

questions.question: क्षुधार्तः means
questions.answer: tormented by hunger
questions.explanation: क्षुधा (hunger) + आर्तः (afflicted) = hungry, hunger-stricken.

questions.question: The word जीर्णम्, describing Somadatta's house, means
questions.answer: old and dilapidated
questions.explanation: जीर्णम् = worn out, decayed — the visible fruit of his idleness.

questions.question: सस्यश्यामलम्, describing Dharmapala's field, means
questions.answer: dark green with crops
questions.explanation: सस्यैः श्यामलम् — (dark-)green with standing crops; the fruit of his labour.

questions.question: निष्कासितवान् means
questions.answer: turned out, expelled
questions.explanation: Somadatta निष्कासितवान् (turned away) the hungry guest — the opposite of अतिथिसत्कार.

questions.question: The शब्दार्थ of श्रद्धया is
questions.answer: with faith/devotion
questions.explanation: श्रद्धा = faith; श्रद्धया is its instrumental (तृतीया) — 'with faith'.

questions.question: In Gita 2.47, the word कदाचन means
questions.answer: ever / at any time
questions.explanation: मा फलेषु कदाचन = 'never (let your claim be) on the fruits'.

questions.question: In Gita 18.46, ततम् means
questions.answer: pervaded
questions.explanation: येन सर्वम् इदं ततम् = 'by whom all this is pervaded' (तन् 'to stretch/pervade').

questions.question: In the Isha Upanishad verse, जिजीविषेत् means
questions.answer: one should wish to live
questions.explanation: Desiderative of जीव् ('to live') in विधिलिङ्: 'should desire to live'.

questions.question: In the subhashita उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति..., मनोरथैः means
questions.answer: by mere wishes/daydreams
questions.explanation: मनोरथः literally 'mind-chariot' = a wish, daydream; the verse opposes wishes to उद्यम (effort).

questions.question: 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन' is a famous verse from
questions.answer: भगवद्गीता (2.47)
questions.explanation: It is Bhagavad Gita 2.47, the classic statement of निष्काम कर्म.

questions.question: According to कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते, a person's rightful claim (अधिकारः) extends to
options: the work alone, never its fruits
the fruits alone, never the work
questions.answer: the work alone, never its fruits
questions.explanation: ते कर्मणि एव अधिकारः, मा फलेषु कदाचन.

questions.question: The closing warning of Gita 2.47, मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि, cautions against
options: attachment to inaction (using detachment as an excuse for idleness)
questions.answer: attachment to inaction (using detachment as an excuse for idleness)
questions.explanation: अकर्मणि सङ्गः मा अस्तु — do not become attached to NOT working; exactly Somadatta's error.

questions.question: Complete Gita 3.19: 'तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म ____'.
questions.answer: समाचर
questions.explanation: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर — 'perform well the work that ought to be done'.

questions.question: According to Gita 3.19, the person who performs action WITHOUT attachment (असक्तः) attains
questions.answer: परम् (the Highest)
questions.explanation: असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः — unattached action leads to the Supreme.

questions.question: 'स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः' occurs in
questions.answer: भगवद्गीता 18.46
questions.explanation: Gita 18.46 — worship through one's own work brings सिद्धि.

questions.question: In Gita 18.46, the instrument by which a person worships the all-pervading Lord is
questions.answer: स्वकर्मणा — by one's own work
questions.explanation: स्वकर्मणा तम् अभ्यर्च्य — one's own honest duty is the offering.

questions.question: In Gita 18.46, what does the worshipper attain by worshipping through his own work?
questions.answer: सिद्धिम् (perfection/fulfilment)
questions.explanation: सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः — a human being finds perfection.

questions.question: 'कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः' is the second mantra of
questions.answer: ईशावास्योपनिषद्
questions.explanation: Isha Upanishad, mantra 2 — the Vedic charter of the working life.

questions.question: For how long does the Isha Upanishad verse say one should wish to live, doing works?
options: as long as the gods permit
questions.answer: a hundred years (शतं समाः)
questions.explanation: जिजीविषेत् शतं समाः — desire to live a hundred years, working.

questions.question: According to Isha Upanishad 2 (न कर्म लिप्यते नरे), action does not stain the doer when
options: life is lived in the spirit the mantra prescribes — working without selfish clinging
the work is done at night
questions.answer: life is lived in the spirit the mantra prescribes — working without selfish clinging
questions.explanation: एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति — living 'thus' (working in the right spirit), karma does not cling to the person.

questions.question: The image of the sleeping lion in उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति teaches that
options: even the mightiest must act — food does not come to the idle
questions.answer: even the mightiest must act — food does not come to the idle
questions.explanation: Deer do not walk into a sleeping lion's mouth: effort is the universal condition of success.

questions.question: कर्मयोगः, as presented in this chapter, is best defined as
options: doing one's duty skilfully and sincerely without attachment to results
working only when rewards are guaranteed
questions.answer: doing one's duty skilfully and sincerely without attachment to results
questions.explanation: Karma-yoga = disciplined, detached, dutiful action offered as worship.

questions.question: A shopkeeper who serves customers honestly and treats fair dealing itself as devotion is following
options: the ideal of स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य — worship through one's own work
the path of Somadatta — outward display
questions.answer: the ideal of स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य — worship through one's own work
questions.explanation: Any honest occupation done with shraddha becomes worship — the chapter's teaching applied to trade.

questions.question: A student says: 'I will study only if I am certain of first rank.' Which correction does the chapter offer?
options: Work is your right and duty; the fruit is not your claim — study sincerely without bargaining for results
Abandon studies since results are uncertain
Demand the rank first, then study
Perform a ritual instead of studying
questions.answer: Work is your right and duty; the fruit is not your claim — study sincerely without bargaining for results
questions.explanation: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते corrects fruit-driven bargaining: do the duty; let results follow.

questions.question: Someone mocks sanitation workers as doing 'low' work. The chapter's reply would be:
options: No honest work is low — labour done sincerely has dignity and is itself worship
Manual work should be avoided by the educated
Mockery is acceptable if done privately
questions.answer: No honest work is low — labour done sincerely has dignity and is itself worship
questions.explanation: श्रमस्य गौरवम् — the dignity of labour — directly refutes contempt for manual work.

questions.question: निष्कामं कर्म (desireless action) means working
options: without selfish craving for the fruit, yet with full effort and care
questions.answer: without selfish craving for the fruit, yet with full effort and care
questions.explanation: Nishkama karma renounces craving, not competence, wages or effort.

questions.question: Which modern figure best parallels Dharmapala's spirit?
options: A nurse who serves every patient with care, seeing her duty itself as service to God
An official who attends festivals but ignores files for months
A trader who cheats customers but donates loudly to temples
A student who skips classes to organise religious processions
questions.answer: A nurse who serves every patient with care, seeing her duty itself as service to God
questions.explanation: Sincere duty + spirit of service = work as worship; the other options repeat Somadatta's error.

questions.question: The chapter would judge charity done ONLY for publicity as
options: another form of बाह्याडम्बर — show without true spirit of service
questions.answer: another form of बाह्याडम्बर — show without true spirit of service
questions.explanation: The test is inner shraddha and real service, not visibility.

questions.question: According to the chapter, the workplace of a sincere worker becomes
options: an altar — the place of worship itself
inferior to a temple in every way
questions.answer: an altar — the place of worship itself
questions.explanation: Where honest effort is poured with shraddha, there worship happens — field, wheel, loom or desk.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of एतद् उपास्यम् is
questions.answer: एतत् + उपास्यम्
questions.explanation: Final त् voices to द् before the vowel उ (जश्त्व-सन्धि).

questions.question: तस्मादसक्तः is correctly split as
questions.answer: तस्मात् + असक्तः
questions.explanation: जश्त्व: त् → द् before अ; तस्मात् (from that/therefore) + असक्तः (unattached).

questions.question: कर्मण्येवाधिकारः involves which sandhi between कर्मणि and एव?
questions.answer: यण्-सन्धि (इ + ए → ये)
questions.explanation: कर्मणि + एव → कर्मण्येव: the इ becomes य् before the dissimilar vowel ए.

questions.question: नान्यथा is correctly split as
questions.answer: न + अन्यथा
questions.explanation: दीर्घ-सन्धि: अ + अ = आ, as in न + अस्ति = नास्ति.

questions.question: The विग्रह of कर्मयोगः as कर्मणा योगः makes it a
questions.answer: तृतीया-तत्पुरुष समास
questions.explanation: 'Union THROUGH action' — the first member carries a hidden instrumental (तृतीया).

questions.question: ग्रामवासिनः (village-dwellers) dissolves as ग्रामे वासिनः, making it a
questions.answer: सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष समास
questions.explanation: 'Dwellers IN the village' — hidden locative (सप्तमी) in the first member.

questions.question: In the sentence क्षुधितेभ्यः अन्नं ददाति, the word क्षुधितेभ्यः is in which vibhakti, and why?
options: चतुर्थी — the recipient of giving takes the dative
questions.answer: चतुर्थी — the recipient of giving takes the dative
questions.explanation: With दान (giving), the receiver stands in चतुर्थी: 'gives food TO the hungry'.

questions.question: In स्वकर्मणा तम् अभ्यर्च्य, the form स्वकर्मणा is
questions.answer: तृतीया एकवचन — 'by one's own work'
questions.explanation: कर्मन् is a neuter n-stem; its instrumental singular is कर्मणा.

questions.question: समाचर (in कार्यं कर्म समाचर) is in which लकार?
questions.answer: लोट् (imperative — a command)
questions.explanation: Krishna commands Arjuna: 'perform!' — second person singular लोट् of सम् + आ + चर्.

questions.question: जिजीविषेत् (one should wish to live) is in which लकार/mood?
questions.answer: विधिलिङ् (optative — 'should')
questions.explanation: The -एत् ending marks विधिलिङ्: 'one SHOULD wish to live a hundred years'.

questions.question: The best English rendering of 'मम कृषिः एव मम पूजा' is
options: My farming itself is my worship
questions.answer: My farming itself is my worship
questions.explanation: एव gives the force 'itself/alone': farming AS worship.

questions.question: 'सः प्रातः उत्थाय ईश्वरं क्षणं स्मृत्वा क्षेत्रं गच्छति स्म' translates best as
options: Rising early and remembering God for a moment, he used to go to the field
He rose late and forgot God on the way to the field
God asked him to rise early and buy a field
In the morning the field remembered God
questions.answer: Rising early and remembering God for a moment, he used to go to the field
questions.explanation: उत्थाय and स्मृत्वा are absolutives ('having risen', 'having remembered'); गच्छति स्म = past habitual.

questions.question: In 'मां मा बाधस्व', the words मा बाधस्व mean
questions.answer: do not disturb (me)
questions.explanation: मा + लोट् (बाधस्व) expresses prohibition: 'do not trouble/disturb'.

questions.question: 'कालेन सः ग्रामः समृद्धः अभवत्' means
options: In time, that village became prosperous
The village was prosperous from the beginning
questions.answer: In time, that village became prosperous
questions.explanation: कालेन (instrumental, 'with/in time') + अभवत् (लङ्, 'became').

questions.question: In 'असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः', the participle आचरन् qualifies
questions.answer: पूरुषः — 'the person, WHILE PERFORMING action'
questions.explanation: आचरन् (present participle, nom. masc. sg.) agrees with पूरुषः: the person performing action unattached attains the Highest.

questions.question: The word उपास्यम् in the title is a gerundive meaning 'that which ought to be worshipped'.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: उप + आस् + यत् (कृत्य-प्रत्यय) = 'worthy of / fit to be worshipped'.

questions.question: In the story, Dharmapala turned the hungry sannyasi away from his field.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: It was Somadatta who turned the guest away; Dharmapala set down his plough and fed him.

questions.question: Somadatta's field was green with crops because of his daily puja.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: His field was dry (शुष्कम्); it was Dharmapala's field that was सस्यश्यामलम् — through labour, not ritual.

questions.question: The story teaches that all prayer and japa are useless.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Dharmapala himself remembers God and does japa; the story condemns only ritual show EMPTY of work and compassion.

questions.question: The word संन्यासी means a renunciant monk.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: संन्यासी = one who has renounced worldly life; the impartial judge of the story.

questions.question: Gita 2.47 permits attachment to inaction as long as one is detached from the fruits of action.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly forbids it: मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि — let there be no attachment to inaction.

questions.question: The verse स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य teaches that one can worship God through one's own work.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Gita 18.46: worshipping the all-pervading Lord by one's own work, a person attains perfection.

questions.question: According to the chapter's ideal, a person doing so-called 'humble' manual work with sincerity stands higher than an idle person performing elaborate rituals.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The dignity of labour: sincere work is worship; idle show is व्यर्थ — as the sannyasi's verdict proves.

questions.question: In एतद् उपास्यम्, the final त् of एतत् changes to द् by जश्त्व-सन्धि.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: A voiceless stop voices before a vowel: एतत् + उपास्यम् → एतद् उपास्यम्.

questions.question: The sentence 'श्रमः एव मन्त्रः' means 'labour itself is the mantra'.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: एव adds the force 'itself': labour is (as good as) the sacred formula.

questions.question: धर्मपुरं नाम रम्यः ________ आसीत् । (Fill in: the story is set in a lovely ...)
questions.answer: ग्रामः
questions.explanation: धर्मपुरं नाम रम्यः ग्रामः आसीत् — 'there was a lovely VILLAGE named Dharmapura'.

questions.question: धर्मपालः ________ चालयन् एव मनसा जपं करोति स्म । (Which implement was he driving?)
questions.answer: हलम्
questions.explanation: सः हलं चालयन् — driving the PLOUGH he did japa in his mind.

questions.question: तत् श्रुत्वा सोमदत्तः ________ अभवत् । (How did Somadatta feel on hearing the sannyasi's words?)
questions.answer: लज्जितः
questions.explanation: सोमदत्तः लज्जितः अभवत् — he became ASHAMED, and then reformed.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'farmer' used in the story is ________ ।
questions.answer: कृषकः
questions.explanation: धर्मपालः नाम कृषकः — Dharmapala the farmer.

questions.question: In Dharmapala's words, 'स्वेदबिन्दवः एव ________' — his sweat-drops themselves are the flowers of worship.
questions.answer: पुष्पाणि
questions.explanation: स्वेदबिन्दवः एव पुष्पाणि — sweat-drops are the FLOWERS.

questions.question: The sannyasi said: कर्म एव ________, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना ।
questions.answer: पूजा
questions.explanation: कर्म एव पूजा — work itself is WORSHIP: the chapter's motto.

questions.question: कर्मणा सेवया च विना बाह्याडम्बरः ________ । (Without work and service, outward show is ...)
questions.answer: व्यर्थः
questions.explanation: बाह्याडम्बरः व्यर्थः — outward display is USELESS.

questions.question: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा ________ कदाचन । (Gita 2.47)
questions.answer: फलेषु
questions.explanation: 'Your right is to the work alone, never to the FRUITS' — फलेषु (locative plural).

questions.question: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म ________ । (Gita 3.19)
questions.answer: समाचर
questions.explanation: समाचर (लोट्) — 'perform well the work that ought to be done'.

questions.question: स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य ________ विन्दति मानवः । (Gita 18.46)
questions.answer: सिद्धिम्
questions.explanation: Worshipping Him by one's own work, a person attains PERFECTION — सिद्धिम्.

questions.question: उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न ________ । (subhashita)
questions.answer: मनोरथैः
questions.explanation: Tasks succeed by effort, not by WISHES/daydreams — मनोरथैः.

questions.question: कुर्वन्नेवेह ________ जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः । (Isha Upanishad 2)
questions.answer: कर्माणि
questions.explanation: 'Doing WORKS alone should one wish to live here a hundred years' — कर्माणि.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: एतद् उपास्यम् = ________ + उपास्यम् ।
questions.answer: एतत्
questions.explanation: जश्त्व-सन्धि: एतत् + उपास्यम् → एतद् उपास्यम्.

questions.question: समास-विग्रह: कर्मयोगः = ________ योगः ।
questions.answer: कर्मणा
questions.explanation: कर्मणा योगः — union THROUGH action (तृतीया-तत्पुरुष).

questions.question: The gerundive of उप + आस् ('worthy of worship'), formed with the यत् suffix, is ________ ।
questions.answer: उपास्यम्
questions.explanation: उप + आस् + यत् = उपास्यम् — the title word itself.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the title एतद् उपास्यम्, and what does the chapter identify as truly worthy of worship?
questions.answer: The title means 'THIS is worthy of worship'. The chapter identifies honest work itself as the true object of worship: कर्म एव पूजा. The sannyasi points to the farmer's work-sanctified plough and sweat-moistened earth and declares that sincere labour, done with faith and flowing into service, deserves the reverence usually given to ritual objects.
questions.explanation: Title meaning + the chapter's thesis.

questions.question: Explain the grammatical formation of उपास्यम् and give one more word formed with the same kind of suffix.
questions.answer: उपास्यम् is a gerundive (कृत्य form): उप + आस् ('to sit near, worship, serve') + the suffix यत्, giving 'that which ought to be worshipped'. Similar gerundives: कार्यम् (कृ + ण्यत्, 'ought to be done'), कर्तव्यम् (कृ + तव्यत्), करणीयम् (कृ + अनीयर्), पठितव्यम् ('ought to be read').
questions.explanation: कृत्य-प्रत्यय yields the sense of obligation/worthiness.

questions.question: What is meant by श्रमस्य गौरवम् (the dignity of labour)? How does the chapter uphold it?
questions.answer: श्रमस्य गौरवम् means that honest physical or mental labour has inherent dignity — no honest work is 'low', and workers deserve respect. The chapter upholds it in three ways: (1) the hero is a farmer whose plough and sweat are declared worthy of worship; (2) Somadatta's contempt for work ('कर्म तु सामान्यजनानां कृते') is shown to be false pride that ruins his household; (3) the verses (स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य, कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि) give scriptural authority to work as a sacred duty.
questions.explanation: Definition plus three supports from story and verses.

questions.question: How did Somadatta spend his day, and what did he say about work?
questions.answer: From morning till evening Somadatta performed only showy worship — loudly ringing the bell, offering flowers and reciting mantras — while doing no work at all. He said with pride: 'अहम् एव सत्यः भक्तः । कर्म तु सामान्यजनानां कृते' — 'I alone am the true devotee; work is for ordinary people.'
questions.explanation: His routine (बाह्याडम्बर) and his contempt for labour.

questions.question: Narrate the sannyasi's visit to the two households and what he found at each.
questions.answer: Hungry, the sannyasi first went to Somadatta's house; Somadatta said 'this is my puja time, do not disturb me' and turned him away. He then went to Dharmapala's field, where he saw earth watered by labour, well-fed cattle and cheerful workers; Dharmapala himself set down his plough, honoured the guest and gave him food and water.
questions.explanation: The two visits form the story's practical test of true devotion.

questions.question: What change came over Somadatta and the village at the end of the story?
questions.answer: Hearing the sannyasi's verdict, Somadatta was ashamed (लज्जितः अभवत्) and from that very day began to do his work sincerely, with shraddha. As a result, in time the whole village of Dharmapura became prosperous (समृद्धः अभवत्).
questions.explanation: The reform of the ritualist and the communal fruit of sincere work.

questions.question: Explain the sannyasi's three equations: कर्म एव पूजा, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना ।
questions.answer: (1) कर्म एव पूजा — work itself is worship: sincere duty replaces the ritual offering. (2) श्रमः एव मन्त्रः — labour itself is the mantra: the rhythm of honest effort is as sacred as recited formulas. (3) सेवा एव आराधना — service itself is adoration: feeding the hungry and honouring guests is the real act of devotion. Together they redefine worship as sincerity-in-action rather than outward display.
questions.explanation: Each equation replaces an element of ritual (पूजा, मन्त्र, आराधना) with an element of working life.

questions.question: Why did the sannyasi judge Dharmapala, and not Somadatta, to be the true worshipper?
questions.answer: Because devotion was tested by action: Somadatta's loud puja could not even spare food for a hungry guest — his ritual was outward show (बाह्याडम्बर) hiding idleness and pride. Dharmapala worked with faith, remembered God while working, and interrupted his ploughing to feed the guest. The sannyasi therefore declared that he who does his own work with श्रद्धा is the true उपासक.
questions.explanation: Action and service, not display, are the measure of worship.

questions.question: The story does not reject devotion; it redefines it. Justify this statement with evidence from the text.
questions.answer: Evidence that devotion is retained: Dharmapala rises early and remembers God (ईश्वरं स्मृत्वा), does japa while ploughing, and speaks of his farming AS puja — he is a devotee. Evidence of redefinition: the sannyasi's verdict transfers the vocabulary of ritual to work (कर्म एव पूजा, श्रमः एव मन्त्रः, सेवा एव आराधना) and declares show without work useless. So the story rejects only empty ritualism (Somadatta's बाह्याडम्बर), while presenting work-with-faith as the higher form of the SAME devotion.
questions.explanation: Distinguishes rejection of ritual-show from redefinition of worship.

questions.question: Give the English शब्दार्थ of: न्यवसत्, जीर्णम्, अतिथिः, समृद्धः.
questions.answer: न्यवसत् = lived, dwelt; जीर्णम् = old, dilapidated; अतिथिः = guest; समृद्धः = prosperous.
questions.explanation: Story vocabulary.

questions.question: Give the English शब्दार्थ of these words from the verses: असक्तः, सततम्, अभ्यर्च्य, विन्दति.
questions.answer: असक्तः = unattached; सततम् = always, constantly; अभ्यर्च्य = having worshipped; विन्दति = attains, finds.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary of Gita 3.19 and 18.46.

questions.question: Distinguish the meanings of the near-synonyms used in the chapter: पूजा, आराधना, उपासना.
questions.answer: पूजा = the concrete act of worship/offering (flowers, bell, mantra — or, in the chapter, work itself). आराधना = adoration, devoted propitiation — worship as loving service (सेवा एव आराधना). उपासना (root of उपास्यम्) = literally 'sitting near' — devoted attendance/meditative service on the worthy object. All three converge in the chapter's message: sincere work with faith performs all of them at once.
questions.explanation: Fine vocabulary discrimination expected at senior-secondary level.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of 'तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर' and translate it.
questions.answer: अन्वय: तस्मात् असक्तः (सन्) सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । Translation: 'Therefore, (being) unattached, always perform well the work that ought to be done.' कार्यम् here is a gerundive qualifying कर्म — 'the to-be-done work', i.e. obligatory duty.
questions.explanation: Anvaya rearranges the verse into prose order; कार्यं कर्म = obligatory action.

questions.question: Explain the two halves of Gita 2.47 and show that together they rule out BOTH greed and idleness.
questions.answer: First half: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits; this rules out greed, working only for reward. Second half: मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि — do not become one motivated by the fruit, and do not be attached to inaction; this rules out idleness, including 'spiritual' idleness disguised as detachment. The verse thus demands full effort with zero bargaining — exactly Dharmapala's way, and the refutation of Somadatta's.
questions.explanation: Both prohibitions (fruit-motivation and inaction) must be identified.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of Isha Upanishad 2 (कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि...) and state its teaching in one sentence.
questions.answer: अन्वय: इह कर्माणि कुर्वन् एव शतं समाः जिजीविषेत् । एवं त्वयि (सति) इतः अन्यथा न अस्ति, (एवं) नरे कर्म न लिप्यते । Teaching: one should desire a long life of a hundred years precisely IN ORDER to keep working; work done in this spirit does not bind or stain the doer.
questions.explanation: The mantra sanctifies lifelong work — the Vedic ideal of श्रम.

questions.question: Which verse of the chapter is closest in meaning to the proverb 'God helps those who help themselves'? Quote it and explain briefly.
questions.answer: उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः । न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥ Tasks are accomplished by effort, not by wishes: even the lion, king of beasts, gets no food while sleeping. Success requires one's own exertion first.
questions.explanation: The subhashita on उद्यम matches the proverb's sense.

questions.question: How would the chapter's teaching change a student's attitude to (a) examinations and (b) household chores?
questions.answer: (a) Examinations: study becomes स्वकर्म done with shraddha — full, regular effort without anxious bargaining over results (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते); marks are the fruit, not the motive, so effort stays steady and anxiety falls. (b) Household chores: sweeping, cooking or washing are not 'low' tasks to be avoided; done sincerely they carry the dignity of labour and are themselves a form of worship and service to the family — as Dharmapala's ploughing was.
questions.explanation: Application of निष्काम कर्म and श्रमस्य गौरवम् to daily student life.

questions.question: Point out ONE similarity and ONE difference between Somadatta's puja and Dharmapala's japa.
questions.answer: Similarity: both are outward acts of religion — both men invoke God daily. Difference: Somadatta's puja is loud display that replaces work and excludes compassion (he turns away the hungry guest), while Dharmapala's japa is silent remembrance that accompanies work and flows into service (he feeds the guest). The form is similar; the spirit and the fruit are opposite.
questions.explanation: Same religious form, opposite inner spirit — the story's key discrimination.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) कर्मण्येव (b) ह्याचरन्.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव — यण्-सन्धि (इ + ए → ये: the इ becomes य् before a dissimilar vowel). (b) ह्याचरन् = हि + आचरन् — यण्-सन्धि (इ + आ → या).
questions.explanation: Both show यण्: इ/ई → य् before a dissimilar vowel.

questions.question: Dissolve and name the samasa: (a) स्वेदबिन्दवः (b) बाह्याडम्बरः (c) क्षुधार्तः.
questions.answer: (a) स्वेदबिन्दवः = स्वेदस्य बिन्दवः ('drops OF sweat') — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. (b) बाह्याडम्बरः = बाह्यः (च असौ) आडम्बरः ('outward show': adjective + noun) — कर्मधारयः. (c) क्षुधार्तः = क्षुधा आर्तः ('afflicted BY hunger') — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः.
questions.explanation: The hidden relation between members names the compound type.

questions.question: Identify the लकार of each verb and translate: (a) अपश्यत् (b) समाचर (c) जिजीविषेत् (d) करोति.
questions.answer: (a) अपश्यत् — लङ् (past): 'he saw'. (b) समाचर — लोट् (imperative): 'perform!'. (c) जिजीविषेत् — विधिलिङ् (optative): 'one should wish to live'. (d) करोति — लट् (present): 'he does/makes'.
questions.explanation: The four लकाराः highlighted by the lesson: लङ्, लोट्, विधिलिङ्, लट्.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'धर्मपालः स्वयं हलं त्यक्त्वा अतिथिं सत्कृत्य अन्नं पानीयं च अददात् ।'
questions.answer: 'Dharmapala himself, having set down the plough and having honoured the guest, gave (him) food and water.' The absolutives त्यक्त्वा ('having left/set down') and सत्कृत्य ('having honoured') show the sequence of actions before the main verb अददात् (gave, लङ्).
questions.explanation: Two क्त्वा/ल्यप् absolutives + past main verb; the sentence embodies अतिथिसत्कार.

questions.question: 'The title एतद् उपास्यम् is itself a compressed lesson in both grammar and philosophy.' Elaborate this statement.
questions.answer:
Grammatically the title teaches two things. First, सन्धि: एतत् + उपास्यम् → एतद् उपास्यम्, where the voiceless त् becomes voiced द् before the vowel उ (जश्त्व). Second, कृत्य-प्रत्यय: उपास्यम् is a gerundive — उप + आस् + यत् — meaning 'that which OUGHT to be worshipped', parallel to कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्. So even before the story begins, the title exercises the student in sandhi-splitting and gerundive recognition.
Philosophically, the title is a pointed answer to an unasked question — 'what deserves worship?' The neuter एतद् ('THIS') points not to a god's image or a person but to a thing present before the eyes: in the story, the farmer's work-sanctified plough and sweat-moistened earth. The gerundive adds the force of obligation: work is not merely respectable, it OUGHT to be revered. Thus the two words compress the whole chapter: कर्म एव पूजा — honest labour, done with faith, is the true object of worship, and labour itself has dignity (श्रमस्य गौरवम्).
questions.explanation: Expected: जश्त्व-सन्धि + यत्-gerundive on the grammar side; the deictic neuter एतद् and work-as-worship on the philosophy side.

questions.question: Narrate the complete story of Somadatta and Dharmapala in your own words, in proper sequence, ending with the sannyasi's verdict and its result.
questions.answer:
In the village of Dharmapura lived Somadatta, who spent every day in loud, showy worship — ringing the bell, offering flowers, reciting mantras — but did no work; his field was dry, his house dilapidated and his family miserable, yet he proudly called himself the only true devotee and said work was for ordinary people. In the same village lived the farmer Dharmapala, who rose early, remembered God for a moment and worked his field, doing japa in his mind while ploughing; he called his farming his puja and his sweat-drops his flowers. His field was green, his family content, and he fed the hungry and honoured guests.
One day a sannyasi came. The villagers asked him which of the two was the better worshipper. Testing them, the hungry sannyasi went first to Somadatta, who turned him away saying it was his puja time. At Dharmapala's field he saw labour-watered earth, well-fed cattle and cheerful workers, and Dharmapala himself put down his plough and served him food and water. The sannyasi then pointed to the work-sanctified plough and declared to the villagers: 'एतद् उपास्यम् — THIS is worthy of worship. He who does his own work with shraddha is the true worshipper; work is puja, labour is the mantra, service is adoration; without work and service outward show is useless.' Somadatta, ashamed, began working sincerely from that day, and in time the village prospered.
questions.explanation: Full sequence: two characters, the test at both homes, the verdict एतद् उपास्यम्, Somadatta's reform, village prosperity.

questions.question: Analyse how the story uses CONTRAST as its chief literary device. Give at least four contrasting pairs from the text and explain what each contributes to the theme.
questions.answer:
The story is built on systematic contrast between the two men. (1) Activity: Somadatta's noisy ritual (घण्टां वादयति, उच्चैः मन्त्रान् पठति) versus Dharmapala's silent japa while ploughing — showing that true devotion is inward, not loud. (2) Results at home: शुष्कं क्षेत्रम्, जीर्णं गृहम्, दुःखितं कुटुम्बम् versus सस्यश्यामलं क्षेत्रम्, स्वच्छं गृहम्, सन्तुष्टं कुटुम्बम् — the visible fruits testify to the worth of each man's 'worship'. (3) Treatment of the guest: Somadatta expels the hungry sannyasi ('मां मा बाधस्व') versus Dharmapala interrupts his work to feed him — service, not ritual, is the real test. (4) Attitude to work: 'कर्म तु सामान्यजनानां कृते' (contempt) versus 'मम कृषिः एव मम पूजा' (reverence) — pride against humility. (5) Even their names contrast subtly: Dharmapala 'protector of dharma' actually protects dharma by action.
Through these mirrored pairs the story makes its judgment inevitable before the sannyasi utters it: wherever the reader looks — sound versus silence, decay versus abundance, cruelty versus kindness — empty ritualism fails and sincere work shines, so the verdict एतद् उपास्यम् lands with full force.
questions.explanation: Any four textual contrasts with their thematic function earn full marks.

questions.question: Prepare a glossary of TEN important words from this chapter (story and verses), giving for each the Devanagari word, its English meaning, and one phrase from the lesson where it occurs.
questions.answer: 1. हलम् — plough — कर्मपूतं हलम्. 2. बाह्याडम्बरः — outward show — बाह्याडम्बरेण पूजाम् एव करोति स्म. 3. स्वेदबिन्दवः — drops of sweat — स्वेदबिन्दवः एव पुष्पाणि. 4. श्रद्धया — with faith — यः स्वकर्म श्रद्धया करोति. 5. क्षुधार्तः — tormented by hunger — सः क्षुधार्तः सोमदत्तस्य गृहं गतवान्. 6. आराधना — adoration/worship — सेवा एव आराधना. 7. असक्तः — unattached — तस्मादसक्तः सततं (गीता 3.19). 8. स्वकर्मणा — by one's own work — स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य (गीता 18.46). 9. उद्यमेन — by effort — उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि. 10. समृद्धः — prosperous — ग्रामः समृद्धः अभवत्.
questions.explanation: Any ten correct word–meaning–context triples from the lesson merit full marks.

questions.question: Write Gita 18.46 and Isha Upanishad 2 with their अन्वय and translation, and explain how together they form the scriptural foundation of 'work is worship'.
questions.answer:
गीता 18.46: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥ अन्वय: यतः भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः, येन इदं सर्वं ततम्, तं स्वकर्मणा अभ्यर्च्य मानवः सिद्धिं विन्दति । Translation: Worshipping, through one's own work, Him from whom beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
ईशावास्योपनिषद् 2: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥ अन्वय: इह कर्माणि कुर्वन् एव शतं समाः जिजीविषेत् ; एवं त्वयि इतः अन्यथा न अस्ति ; नरे कर्म न लिप्यते । Translation: Doing works alone should one wish to live here a hundred years; for you there is no other way; (thus) action does not stain the doer.
Together they ground 'work is worship' from both ends. The Gita verse supplies the POSITIVE claim: one's own duty (स्वकर्म) is itself a valid offering to the all-pervading Lord — the workplace becomes the altar, and its reward is सिद्धि. The Upanishad supplies the CHARTER for a working life: far from being a fall from spirituality, a full hundred years of work is the prescribed human path, and work so done leaves no stain. One verse makes work sacred; the other makes it lifelong and liberating — precisely what Dharmapala's plough demonstrates in the story.
questions.explanation: Both verses with anvaya + the complementary argument (work as offering; work as lifelong stainless path).

questions.question: 'In modern society we garland the idols but look down on those who sweep the streets.' Evaluate this attitude in the light of this chapter, and suggest three concrete ways a young person can practise श्रमस्य गौरवम् today.
questions.answer:
The chapter would condemn this attitude as Somadatta's error writ large: reverence directed at the symbols of religion while the living carriers of service — farmers, sweepers, masons, sanitation and delivery workers — are treated with contempt. The sannyasi's verdict inverts that hierarchy: the plough sanctified by work (कर्मपूतं हलम्) deserves the garland, for कर्म एव पूजा and सेवा एव आराधना. Gita 18.46 removes any scriptural excuse for contempt: EVERY honest स्वकर्म is a valid worship of the Lord; hence no honest worker is 'lower' than a priest. A society that honours display but humiliates labour is, by the story's logic, worshipping the wrong object — and impoverishing itself, as Somadatta impoverished his own house.
Three concrete practices: (1) Speak and behave respectfully with all workers — thank the sweeper, the bus conductor, the canteen staff by name, and never use occupation as an insult. (2) Do one's own share of manual work — clean one's room, wash one's plate, join campus/community cleanliness drives — so that labour is experienced, not merely praised. (3) Do one's own duty (study, job) with full sincerity and without bargaining for reward, treating it as one's daily puja — and support fair treatment and fair wages for those who labour.
questions.explanation: Evaluation using the story + Gita, then any three sensible practices.

questions.question: From the lesson, give (a) three sandhi examples with their split and rule-name, (b) three samasa examples with विग्रह and type, and (c) one verb form each in लट्, लङ्, लोट् and विधिलिङ् with meaning.
questions.answer:
(a) सन्धि: 1. एतद् उपास्यम् = एतत् + उपास्यम् (जश्त्व — त् → द् before a vowel). 2. कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (यण् — इ → य् before ए). 3. नान्यथा = न + अन्यथा (दीर्घ — अ + अ = आ). (Also acceptable: तस्मादसक्तः = तस्मात् + असक्तः, जश्त्व; जिजीविषेच्छतम् = जिजीविषेत् + शतम्, श्चुत्व.)
(b) समास: 1. कर्मयोगः = कर्मणा योगः — तृतीया-तत्पुरुष. 2. ग्रामवासिनः = ग्रामे वासिनः — सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष. 3. बाह्याडम्बरः = बाह्यः आडम्बरः — कर्मधारय. (Also: स्वेदबिन्दवः = स्वेदस्य बिन्दवः, षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; क्षुधार्तः = क्षुधा आर्तः, तृतीया-तत्पुरुष.)
(c) लकाराः: लट् — करोति 'he does' (सः कर्म करोति). लङ् — अभवत् 'he became' (लज्जितः अभवत्). लोट् — समाचर 'perform!' (कार्यं कर्म समाचर). विधिलिङ् — जिजीविषेत् 'one should wish to live' (शतं समाः जिजीविषेत्).
questions.explanation: Any correct three + three + four with names and meanings.

questions.question: Compose FIVE simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) on the theme 'कर्म एव पूजा', using at least one लोट् form, one absolutive (क्त्वा/ल्यप्), and one तृतीया form. Give the English meaning of each sentence.
questions.answer: Model answer: 1. श्रद्धया स्वकर्म कुरु । (Do your own work with faith — लोट् कुरु; तृतीया श्रद्धया.) 2. कृषकः क्षेत्रं गत्वा हलं चालयति । (The farmer, having gone to the field, drives the plough — absolutive गत्वा.) 3. श्रमेण एव जीवनं सफलं भवति । (By labour alone does life become fruitful — तृतीया श्रमेण.) 4. वयं क्षुधितेभ्यः अन्नं दद्मः । (We give food to the hungry.) 5. आलस्यं त्यक्त्वा उद्यमं कुर्यात् । (Having abandoned laziness, one should make effort — absolutive त्यक्त्वा, विधिलिङ् कुर्यात्.) Any five grammatically correct sentences on the theme, containing the required forms, deserve full marks.
questions.explanation: Tests free composition with specified grammar: लोट्, absolutive, तृतीया.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'सः प्रातःकालात् सायंकालपर्यन्तं बाह्याडम्बरेण पूजाम् एव करोति स्म — उच्चैः घण्टां वादयति स्म, पुष्पाणि अर्पयति स्म, मन्त्रान् च पठति स्म । परन्तु सः किमपि कर्म न करोति स्म ।'
(a) Who is described here? (b) List the three acts of his 'worship'. (c) What single fact undercuts all of them?
questions.answer: (a) Somadatta of Dharmapura. (b) He loudly rang the bell (घण्टां वादयति स्म), offered flowers (पुष्पाणि अर्पयति स्म) and recited mantras (मन्त्रान् पठति स्म). (c) The fact that he did no work at all (किमपि कर्म न करोति स्म) — his worship was mere outward show (बाह्याडम्बर) with no labour or service behind it.
questions.explanation: The passage introduces the idle ritualist; the closing परन्तु-clause is the key.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'सोमदत्तः "पूजासमयः अयम् । मां मा बाधस्व" इति उक्त्वा तं निष्कासितवान् । ... धर्मपालः स्वयं हलं त्यक्त्वा अतिथिं सत्कृत्य अन्नं पानीयं च अददात् ।'
(a) Whom did each man face, and in what condition was he? (b) What irony lies in Somadatta's excuse 'पूजासमयः अयम्'? (c) What does Dharmapala's हलं त्यक्त्वा ('setting down the plough') signify?
questions.answer: (a) Both faced the visiting sannyasi, who was tormented by hunger (क्षुधार्तः). (b) The irony: Somadatta refuses to feed a hungry holy guest BECAUSE it is 'worship time' — using worship as a reason to fail the very compassion worship should produce; his puja thus cancels itself. (c) Dharmapala interrupts even his sacred work to serve the guest — showing that in his scale of values service stands highest; work is his worship, and service of the needy is its truest expression (सेवा एव आराधना).
questions.explanation: The paired scene is the story's moral test; the irony of (b) is central.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'ततः संन्यासी धर्मपालस्य कर्मपूतं हलं स्वेदसिक्तां भूमिं च अङ्गुल्या निर्दिश्य अवदत् — "पश्यत! एतद् उपास्यम् ।"'
(a) To which two objects does the sannyasi point? (b) Why does he call THEM, and not an idol, worthy of worship? (c) Which two-word Sanskrit phrase here gives the chapter its title?
questions.answer: (a) To Dharmapala's plough sanctified by work (कर्मपूतं हलम्) and the sweat-moistened earth (स्वेदसिक्तां भूमिम्). (b) Because they are the visible embodiment of sincere labour and service — the true worship; sanctity, he teaches, comes from honest work (कर्म एव पूजा), not from ritual objects. (c) एतद् उपास्यम् — 'THIS is worthy of worship'.
questions.explanation: The climax scene explains and names the title.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥'
(a) From which text and chapter/verse is this? (b) Give the meaning of अधिकारः and अकर्मणि here. (c) State the verse's two prohibitions in your own words.
questions.answer: (a) Bhagavad Gita 2.47. (b) अधिकारः = right, rightful claim/entitlement; अकर्मणि = in inaction, in not-working (locative of अकर्म). (c) Prohibition 1: do not work with the fruit as your motive — never claim or crave the results of action. Prohibition 2: do not become attached to inaction — detachment from results must not become an excuse to stop working.
questions.explanation: Source, two key words, and the double prohibition.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥'
(a) Who is referred to by तम् ('Him')? (b) What is the instrument of worship in this verse, and in which vibhakti does it stand? (c) How does Dharmapala of the story fulfil this verse?
questions.answer: (a) तम् refers to the Lord — He from whom all beings arise (यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानाम्) and by whom all this universe is pervaded (येन सर्वमिदं ततम्). (b) स्वकर्मणा — 'one's own work', in the तृतीया (instrumental) vibhakti: work is the INSTRUMENT of worship. (c) Dharmapala worships precisely through his own work: his farming is his puja, his sweat-drops the flowers; and he 'finds siddhi' — a flourishing field, a content family, and recognition as the true worshipper.
questions.explanation: Identification of तम्, the instrumental स्वकर्मणा, and the story parallel.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥' (ईशावास्योपनिषद् 2)
A retired officer says: 'I have worked for forty years; now religion means giving up all activity.' Using this mantra, evaluate his view.
questions.answer: The mantra prescribes the opposite ideal: one should WISH to live even a hundred years precisely by continuing to do works (कुर्वन्नेव कर्माणि जिजीविषेत् शतं समाः) — it declares there is no other proper way for a human being (नान्यथेतोऽस्ति). Age may rightly change the KIND of work — from office duties to teaching, guiding the young, community service, gardening — but not the fact of working. The mantra also removes his fear that activity binds: done in the right spirit, without selfish clinging, कर्म does not stain the doer (न कर्म लिप्यते नरे). So religion for him should mean purified, selfless activity — Somadatta's error corrected — not the abandonment of activity.
questions.explanation: The mantra's positive command, its 'no other way' clause, and the non-staining promise all refute total inactivity.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer the grammar questions:
'यः स्वकर्म श्रद्धया करोति, सः एव सत्यः उपासकः ।'
(a) State the vibhakti and role of श्रद्धया. (b) What is the relation between यः and सः in this sentence? (c) उपासकः and उपास्यम् come from the same root — distinguish their meanings.
questions.answer: (a) श्रद्धया is तृतीया (instrumental) एकवचन of श्रद्धा — 'WITH faith/devotion', expressing manner. (b) यः ... सः is the relative–correlative pair: 'HE WHO (यः) does his own work with faith, HE alone (सः एव) is the true worshipper.' (c) Both derive from उप + आस्: उपासकः is the agent noun — 'the worshipper, one who worships'; उपास्यम् is the gerundive — 'that which ought to be worshipped, the object of worship'. Doer versus object of the same act.
questions.explanation: Instrumental of manner, यत्-तत् correlation, and agent vs gerundive from one root.

questions.question:
Read and translate, then answer:
'तस्य क्षेत्रं सस्यश्यामलम् आसीत्, गृहं स्वच्छम्, कुटुम्बं च सन्तुष्टम् । सः क्षुधितेभ्यः अन्नं ददाति स्म, अतिथीन् च सत्करोति स्म ।'
(a) Translate the passage into English. (b) Whose household is described? (c) Which value of Indian culture does the second sentence embody?
questions.answer: (a) 'His field was dark-green with crops, his house clean, and his family content. He used to give food to the hungry and honour guests.' (b) Dharmapala's — the sincere farmer. (c) अतिथिसत्कार / अतिथिदेवो भव — hospitality and service: honouring the guest and feeding the hungry as a sacred duty.
questions.explanation: Simple prose translation plus recognition of the hospitality ideal.

questions.question: Case: Ritu is a brilliant Class 12 student. During examination month she stops helping at home, saying 'housework is beneath a scholar', yet she also keeps postponing study, daydreaming about the top rank she will win. Using TWO teachings of this chapter, advise Ritu.
questions.answer: Teaching 1 — श्रमस्य गौरवम् / कर्म एव पूजा: no honest work is 'beneath' anyone. Somadatta thought work was for ordinary people, and his pride ruined his household; helping at home, done with a good spirit, is itself worship and builds character. Ritu should drop the contempt and share the chores she reasonably can. Teaching 2 — उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः, and Gita 2.47: results come from effort, not daydreams, and her right is to the studying itself, not to the rank. Deer do not enter a sleeping lion's mouth; the top rank will not come by imagining it. She should study steadily with shraddha (her स्वकर्म), stop bargaining with the result, and let the fruit follow the work.
questions.explanation: Both errors — contempt for labour and daydreaming instead of effort — matched to chapter teachings.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer the vocabulary questions:
'तत्र सः श्रमेण सिक्तां भूमिं, तृप्तान् पशून्, प्रसन्नान् कर्मकरान् च अपश्यत् ।'
(a) Give the English meaning of सिक्ताम्, तृप्तान् and कर्मकरान्. (b) Who is the 'सः' who saw all this, and where?
questions.answer: (a) सिक्ताम् = moistened/watered; तृप्तान् = satisfied, well-fed; कर्मकरान् = workers, labourers. (b) सः is the visiting sannyasi, and he saw this at Dharmapala's field — earth watered by labour, well-fed cattle and cheerful workers.
questions.explanation: Context-based shabdartha from the field scene.
